History:
- Chief complaint: Acute, severe left-sided headache that woke patient at ~05:30 today (usual wake time 07:00); still present.
- Character/progression: More severe than prior headaches; typically past headaches were less severe and across the forehead; current episode is unilateral (left).
- Associated symptoms: Mild photophobia; brief dizziness on waking (resolved); denies neck stiffness; denies fever; “not really” nauseous.
- Positional: Initially worse on lying down, then improves; overall better when lying down.
- Triggers/context: Significant work-related stress with late nights for ~2 months; sleep likely reduced.
- Analgesics tried: Paracetamol this morning without relief.

Past Medical History:
- Anxiety (~2 years), currently treated.
- No history of hypertension; has not had BP checked previously.
- Family history: Mother with anxiety; no known family history of migraine.
- Medications:
  - Sertraline (dose/route/frequency not documented) — currently taking.
  - Paracetamol taken today for headache (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.
- Social: Non-smoker; lives with partner; exercises (runs ~3x/week); diet “okay”; has a cat.

Physical Examination:
- Telehealth consultation; no vitals or in-person exam performed.
- Reported findings: No neck stiffness; no fever; mild photophobia; dizziness resolved; headache ongoing.

Impression:
- Acute unilateral headache, likely tension-type versus migraine; more severe than prior episodes; no red-flag symptoms reported in transcript.

Management Plan:
- Start ibuprofen as first-line for suspected migraine-type headache (dose/route/frequency not documented); may continue paracetamol if desired (dose/route/frequency not documented). Aspirin discussed as an alternative option per guidelines.
- Stress management: Consider ~1 week off work (self-certify).
- Counseling: Provided link for local counseling service for self-referral to address stress.
- Lifestyle: Aim for 7–8 hours of sleep nightly; hydrate 1.5–2.0 liters of fluids daily (excluding coffee/tea); note fatigue and dehydration can trigger headaches.
- Safety-net: Patient advised to review provided headache red-flag information and seek care urgently if symptoms worsen or new red flags develop.
- Follow-up: Book follow-up in 1 week. If not improving, consider blood tests and reassessment.

Patient Summary:
- Patient with new, severe left-sided headache awakening him early, with mild photophobia and no fever or neck stiffness. Clinical impression is tension-type versus migraine in the context of work-related stress and poor sleep.
- Plan includes trial of ibuprofen, continued symptomatic care, stress reduction (time off, counseling), hydration/sleep optimization, and close follow-up in one week.

Key Takeaways:
- Begin ibuprofen for headache; you may continue paracetamol if needed (doses not documented in transcript).
- Prioritize hydration (1.5–2 L/day) and 7–8 hours of sleep nightly.
- Monitor for headache red flags; seek care if symptoms worsen or new concerning signs appear.

Next Steps:
- Schedule follow-up appointment in 1 week.
- Self-refer to counseling service; consider short work leave to reduce stress.
- If no improvement at follow-up, proceed with blood tests and further evaluation.
